description: BenchKeeper sets up Claude Code and Codex the same way on your machine and in each repository: short global rules and a workflow skill that sizes each task, plus a dev container, `AGENTS.md` and skills per repository. Its app shows every change before it applies it and records each run so you can undo it.

levels.name: Lite
levels.contains: the BenchKeeper plugin: the `workflow`, `ask`, `questions`, `setting-up-projects`, `maintaining-repos`, `orchestrating-projects`, `reviewing-rules`, `audit`, `improve` and `debloat` skills
levels.writes: nothing outside the plugin install, besides the app's run record for undo

levels.name: Standard
levels.contains: lite plus the local project block: `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.override.md` and the git exclude list
levels.writes: local files in each project you run `projects apply` in
levels.command: npx @cedarloom/app@6.27.0 apply --level standard && npx @cedarloom/app@6.27.0 projects apply

levels.name: Full
levels.contains: standard plus the global rules, Claude Code and Codex settings, packs and the app
levels.writes: global rule files, settings and packs

quickstart.needs: Node.js 22 and at least one agent, Claude Code or Codex.
quickstart.choose: Choose the App to review each change in the browser. Choose the CLI in a terminal-only session or in a script.

steps.text: Opens the browser on the Dashboard with the doctor findings (the read-only checks of this machine). Select Fix everything, review the changes and press Apply; nothing is written before.
Lists each change and writes nothing.
Asks per change. `--yes` applies the default selection without questions.

quickstart.next: After either path, restart the agents.
quickstart.changes: `npx @cedarloom/app@6.27.0 history` lists what changed, `npx @cedarloom/app@6.27.0 undo <run>` reverses a run.

prerequisites.name: Claude Code
prerequisites.for: agent, at least one; Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI get rules, skills, settings, doctor and project setup only. Version 2.1.292 or later for the effort a skill passes to a subagent call, such as `xhigh` for a security review: 2.1.267 to 2.1.291 run each subagent at the `effort` of its definition (`high` for the reviewer), and an older one ignores that field on Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8 and Fable 5

prerequisites.name: Codex CLI
prerequisites.for: agent, at least one; Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI get rules, skills, settings, doctor and project setup only

prerequisites.name: GitHub CLI
prerequisites.for: issues and pull requests (optional, local branches without it)

prerequisites.name: Node.js and npm
prerequisites.for: the app (Node.js 22), Dev Containers CLI and skills CLI, npm with a user prefix such as `$HOME/.local`

prerequisites.name: Docker Engine
prerequisites.for: dev containers (`container` and `host-agent` modes; Podman works too)

parallelTools.name: Orca
points: one git worktree per agent, the same prompt across agents
terminal splits, SSH remote worktrees, mobile app

visual editors (Markdown, CSV, mockups, diagrams), task tracking, iOS app

openhands.name: OpenHands
openhands.summary: A self-hosted agent server with a web UI that runs work without you at the terminal.
points: Each conversation can run in its own Docker container (`OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker`), an isolation option BenchKeeper does not provide.
Runs its own agent or hosts Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI.
Automations on a schedule or on webhook events (GitHub, Slack, Linear), for example splitting GitHub issues into tasks.
Without a sandbox, the local agent has full access to your filesystem.
Unverified: whether agents inside its containers load the BenchKeeper rules and skills, which are installed on the host.

sdlc.requirements: Requests come from you, GitHub issues, Jira, Linear and other trackers, bug reports, reviews and Maintain findings. Only GitHub issues are automated.

steps.name: Understand
steps.tip: Reads the request, AGENTS.md and the code it touches, and picks the kind (software change, docs pass, research) and the depth. Standard and deep: open questions go with recommendations into one issue, and the agent goes on (in rounds, then plan mode, while you allow terminal questions).
steps.text: Read the request, `AGENTS.md` and the code the change touches, and pick the kind (software change, docs pass, research) and the depth. Standard and deep: the agent writes the open questions, each with a recommendation, into one issue in the tracker the project names, takes the safe and reversible ones and goes on. Only while you allow terminal questions does it ask them in rounds and explore in plan mode.

steps.name: Specify
steps.tip: Standard: a plan of a few lines that names the test seams. Deep: the spec, terms and decisions recorded. Several sessions: one ticket per testable slice.
steps.text: Standard: a plan of a few lines that names the test seams. Deep: the spec (deployment target, data storage, module boundaries, core types), with terms and decisions recorded. Work for several sessions: one ticket per independently testable slice.

steps.name: Build
steps.tip: Standard and deep: the existing tests of the touched code, then a test first only where the test rule calls for one.
steps.text: Standard and deep: the existing tests that cover the touched code run first, then a test first at the agreed seams only where the test rule calls for one, ticket by ticket. Deep: when the build drifts from the plan, the agent stops and asks before it discards the branch and restarts.

steps.name: Verify
steps.tip: Every depth: build, types, lint and tests where AGENTS.md says, each with its command and result. UI changes also in a browser. Deep: the branch reviewed against the spec.
steps.text: Every depth: the project's build, types, lint and tests, run where `AGENTS.md` says (the dev container by default), each reported with its command and result. UI changes also get a browser check, in addition to the UI tests, never instead of them. Long checks run once, after the last edit. Deep: the branch is reviewed against the spec.

steps.name: Ship
steps.tip: Standard, deep and risky: /code-review before push. Risky: /security-review. Pull request when the project uses them, checks. You merge.
steps.text: Standard, deep and risky work: `/code-review` before `git push` (correctness), risky changes also `/security-review`. When the project uses pull requests, one with the key decisions, then its checks. Merge only on your instruction. Several tasks on one branch get one review at the end.

steps.name: Maintain
steps.tip: On request: /maintaining-repos (audit, cleanup, architecture, test audit, debt, dependencies, pins, docs drift, unused skills). Findings become new requests.
steps.text: On request (`/cl-setup:maintaining-repos`): cleanup tools (unused code, duplicates), architecture checks (cycles, forwarding modules), a test audit by mutation testing, dependency audit, version pins, docs drift, `/doctor prompt-audit`, `/skill-doctor`, repository hygiene. Findings become new requests.

reasons.name: Checks by depth
reasons.text: every change runs the checks and reviews its depth names: the tests of the touched code after each edit, a review before pushing for standard and deep work.

reasons.name: Long checks last
reasons.text: the full suite, end-to-end tests and builds run once after the last edit, in a subagent that returns only failures and key lines.

reasons.name: Simplicity
reasons.text: the optional Ponytail pack adds a plugin that steers the agent to the smallest complete change.

reasons.name: Skills by level
reasons.text: the full flow runs only for deep work. Small changes load one targeted skill.

reasons.name: One install
reasons.text: one machine setup covers every repository. Each repository adds only its tracker, docs and stack.
